name: Mongolia
sources: Inflation: the World Bank publishes no CPI series for Mongolia in 1990. Prices were still administered that year and the explosion came later — official inflation passed 320% in 1992-93. 0.20 is entered as the point at which the administered price system was already visibly failing, with interest at 0.18 to keep the real rate near neutral. Both are constructions, not transcriptions.

tax_rate 0.42 and state investment 0.27 are what a Soviet-model economy looks like in these fields: almost all output passes through the state budget and almost all investment is planned. Neither is a published Mongolian statistic for 1990; both are the shape of a CMEA member's accounts rather than a transcription, and are entered as such.

Debt at 1.0x GDP stands for the transferable-ruble balance owed to the Soviet Union, which Mongolia carried at over 10 billion rubles. That figure has no honest dollar equivalent — Russia and Mongolia argued about it until a 98% write-off in 2003 — so the ratio here is a placeholder for a very large unpayable obligation rather than a measured number.

tfp_trend is negative because Mongolia was the most CMEA-dependent economy in the world outside the Soviet Union: Soviet transfers ran near a third of GDP and stopped. Output fell by roughly a fifth over 1990-1993.

Stability 42 with authoritarianism 0.80: the demonstrations in Sukhbaatar Square began on 10 December 1989 and were running through the month the game opens. The Politburo resigned on 9 March 1990 and Article 82's monopoly clause went with it. In January 1990 the MPRP still had the monopoly, so it is entered as a one-party state that is visibly about to stop being one.
Military index 2: about 25,000 under arms, plus the Soviet 39th Army, whose withdrawal was agreed in 1989 and completed in 1992.
Gross capital formation 29.1% of GDP (World Bank, 1990), entered as 27 state and 2 private, which is what the split looks like in an economy where the plan does the investing.

Series check, August 2026, read from the World Bank API: NY.GDP.MKTP.CD 1990 = 2,560,785,660; SP.POP.TOTL = 2,098,710; MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS = 4.281; NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS = 29.067. All match. FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG and FR.INR.LEND return NO VALUE for Mongolia in 1990, which is the direct confirmation of what this file says above: the inflation and interest figures here are constructions and not transcriptions.

pop_growth_1990 = 2.5341%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series MNG (Mongolia): 1,874,349 in 1984 to 2,124,185 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: MNG.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 84% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: bio_universal_immunisation GRANTED.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 0 against a threshold of any positive count: refused.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.

granted.source: WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 immunisation coverage (% of surviving infants), retrieved from the UNICEF public SDMX API, dataflow UNICEF:IMMUNISATION(1.0), indicator IM_DTP3, DATA_SOURCE field 'WHO/UNICEF estimates of national immunization coverage, 2025 revision'. Series value: MNG, 1990 = 84%, at or above the 80% WHO/UNICEF Universal Childhood Immunization (UCI-1990) target that defines this technology's name.
